To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sequence homology is a consistent feature in mitochondrial DNA deletions, and that the degree of sequence homology is correlated with age of onset, with the highest level in patients over 6 years old, and the lowest in patients under 6 years of age, with multisystem involvement.
sequence homology at mtDNA deletion breakpoints is a common feature, and the level of homology is associated with the clinical features and age at onset of mitochondrial disease.
the sequence homology surrounding the mtDNA deletion breakpoint is a common feature, and that the degree of sequence homology correlates with the age of onset and severity of disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of mtDNA deletion breakpoints and their clinical implications.
the molecular signatures of mtDNA deletional disorders and their association with clinical phenotype and age of onset.
the clinical and genetic aspects of mitochondrial diseases, and the molecular mechanisms of mtDNA deletional pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deletion junctions of mtDNA deletional disorders have a high degree of sequence homology.
the deletion size, the location and the degree of sequence homology at deletion flanking regions, and heteroplasmy levels are all associated with the age of onset and severity of the phenotype.
the clinical presentation and age of onset of mtDNA deletion syndromes are associated with the deletion breakpoint and the levels of deletion mutant mtDNA heteroplasmy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mtDNA deletion syndromes are not a single entity but rather a spectrum of disorders with different age of disease onset, severity, and clinical features.
mtDNA deletions are not a random phenomenon, and there is a strong correlation between deletion location and clinical presentation.
the clinical phenotype is associated with the age of onset and the molecular signature of mtDNA deletional disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sequence homology at deletion breakpoints is a consistent feature and that the clinical features of mtDNA deletion syndrome are associated with the age of onset and the level of sequence homology at breakpoints.

mtDNA deletion breakpoints in the young patients are more heterogeneous and less homologous to mtDNA background than in older patients, suggesting a more complex mechanism in the pathogenesis of mtDNA deletional disease in young patients than in the older patients.
sequence homology is a consistent feature in mtDNA deletion syndromes and that the presence or absence of sequence homology flanks can help predict the clinical phenotype and disease onset.
